## Context / Problem
Nested pytest sessions that execute tests requiring temporary fixtures without a private --basetemp join pytest's user-global numbered root and may delete unrelated cleanup-eligible trees at session finish. The parent pytest process owns the temporary lifetime, so each affected nested child must use a unique basetemp under its parent's tmp_path. This bug was discovered from grindable-deviant-angwantibo after its runtime RCA confirmed that cleanup mechanism.

## Complete nested-pytest inventory
Direct subprocess launch constructs:
- tests/_store_isolation.py:32-48 is safe: it passes tmp_path / nested-pytest as --basetemp.
- tests/unit/test_external_isolation.py:62-78 is safe: it passes tmp_path / bt as --basetemp.
- tests/unit/test_ci_snapshot_fixture_cleanup.py:13-31 is safe: it passes tmp_path / nested-basetemp as --basetemp.
- tests/unit/test_git_version_floor.py:143-178 is non-applicable: --collect-only exits during configuration under the fake under-floor Git and never allocates TempPathFactory._basetemp.
- tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:826-848 is non-applicable: its --collect-only children instantiate no fixtures and never allocate TempPathFactory._basetemp.
- tests/unit/test_tests_import_convention.py:82-116 is non-applicable: its --collect-only children instantiate no fixtures and never allocate TempPathFactory._basetemp.
- tests/unit/test_engine_dir.py:148-204 is confirmed unsafe: it executes the selected reducer test under repository conftest autouse fixtures, allocating the shared numbered root without --basetemp.
- tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py:142-178 is confirmed unsafe: it executes the standalone reproduction module under repository conftest autouse fixtures, allocating the shared numbered root without --basetemp.

Pytester's managed launches are already safe: six pytester.runpytest_subprocess calls in tests/unit/test_caplog_coverage_integrity.py:180-264 receive the helper's native numbered --basetemp, and four pytester.runpytest calls in tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py:158-215 pass through Pytester._ensure_basetemp. The literal pytest occurrences in tests/scripts/test_summarize_ci_failures.py:134 and tests/unit/grounding/test_deps.py:286-298 are test data, not launch sites.

The non-applicable classification follows pytest 9.1's _pytest.tmpdir.TempPathFactory contract inspected in the installed locked dependency: pytest_configure constructs the factory without allocating a root; pytest_sessionfinish returns immediately while _basetemp is None; getbasetemp is what creates and registers cleanup for the numbered root. Therefore a collect-only child that resolves no temporary fixture cannot execute this defect. A repository-wide AST/literal search plus a pytester.runpytest search found no other nested pytest launch sites.

## Approach
Add tmp_path to each of the two confirmed unsafe outer tests and pass a distinct child path through --basetemp. This follows the already-green ownership pattern in tests/_store_isolation.py:32-48 and tests/unit/test_external_isolation.py:62-78, keeps cleanup local to the parent fixture, and preserves each child's interpreter or console-script entrypoint, cwd, selectors, plugins, and assertions. The three collect-only launchers remain unchanged because runtime control flow cannot reach the cleanup mechanism; changing them would not repair a demonstrated defect.

Add a behavior-level real-subprocess regression for the two executing sites. A seed child allocates an isolated PYTEST_DEBUG_TEMPROOT; the test then creates enough unlocked numbered directories to make the seed sentinel cleanup-eligible. The outer subprocess receives its own --basetemp so it cannot touch the shared root. It drives one affected outer test, whose nested child crosses the real numbered-root cleanup seam. The sentinel's exact bytes distinguish the broken and repaired behavior without timing sleeps or source-text assertions.

## Scope
- tests/unit/test_engine_dir.py: parent-owned basetemp for the mixed-module child.
- tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py: parent-owned basetemp for the standalone bare-pytest child.
- tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_basetemp.py: held-out real-subprocess regression for both confirmed cleanup sites.

No production module, dependency, configuration key, or public API changes.

## Testing
- RED oracle: seed an isolated shared numbered root, prove the sentinel is cleanup-eligible, run each affected outer test with an outer --basetemp, and assert its nested child deletes the sentinel before repair.
- GREEN oracle: apply the repair and assert each exact sentinel byte payload remains unchanged.
- Contrast/control: require each driven outer test to return success, preserving its existing entrypoint, cwd, selection, plugin, and assertion contract.
- Mutation: remove one repaired --basetemp pair to restore the exact defect and confirm that site's held-out case returns RED, then restore it.
- Focused: run the new regression plus tests/unit/test_engine_dir.py and tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py.
- Broad: run the CI default unit selection, make lint, and make typecheck.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The inventory classifies every direct and pytester-managed nested pytest launch; verified by repository AST, literal, and pytester.runpytest searches.
- [ ] The engine-directory nested child leaves its cleanup-eligible sentinel byte-for-byte unchanged; verified by its parametrized case in tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_basetemp.py.
- [ ] The standalone import-convention nested child leaves its cleanup-eligible sentinel byte-for-byte unchanged; verified by its parametrized case in tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_basetemp.py.
- [ ] Existing nested entrypoint, cwd, selector, plugin, and child assertions remain green; verified by focused execution of both affected modules.
- [ ] Removing a repaired --basetemp makes the corresponding held-out behavior case fail; verified by the exact-defect mutation run.
- [ ] The CI default unit selection exits zero.
- [ ] make lint exits zero.
- [ ] make typecheck exits zero.
